key_provisions_or_claims: No formal communication process exists between robot developers and regulators from which policy could learn.
Proposes a model linking ex-ante technology impact assessments to legislative ex-post evaluations.
Shared data repositories would enable evidence-based, iterative robot policy learning.
Existing legislation may apply to new robots but new challenges question its applicability.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper arguing there is no formal communication channel between robot developers and regulators for policy learning. It proposes linking ex-ante technology impact assessments with legislative ex-post evaluations through shared data repositories, supporting evidence-based, iterative robot governance.
annotation.title_clean: “Meet Me Halfway,” Said the Robot to the Regulation: Linking Ex-Ante Technology Impact Assessments to Legislative Ex-Post Evaluations via Shared Data Repositories for Robot Governance
annotation.title_en: “Meet Me Halfway,” Said the Robot to the Regulation: Linking Ex-Ante Technology Impact Assessments to Legislative Ex-Post Evaluations via Shared Data Repositories for Robot Governance
annotation.venue: Inclusive Robotics for a Better Society (INBOTS 2018), Springer
